subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity signal, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, parent wake contract, and user-visible notification behavior should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior adds new defaults/config, automatic child-run mutation, and chat-visible recovery semantics for existing deployments, which cannot be chosen safely as a narrow automated bug fix.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity source, nudge and kill behavior, parent wake contract, and channel notification ownership.

options.title: Prototype default-off
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in watchdog first with no upgrade behavior change until live proof and maintainer approval settle defaults.

options.title: Defer to existing controls
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds and manual kill/reap work for now, and revisit automatic recovery after the session activity model lands.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity source, nudge and kill behavior, parent wake contract, and channel notification ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on subagent timeout, stale-run, and killed-run state paths that would own the recovery contract.
